parties: Netweb Technologies India Limited (issuer); qualified institutional buyers (subscribers)
headline: Netweb Technologies allots 2,505,219 shares in QIP
sum: Netweb Technologies India Limited has completed allotment of 2,505,219 securities pursuant to a Qualified Institution Placement (QIP), as intimated to NSE on 20 August 2026 following board approval.
implication: QIP allotment completion signals capital raise closure under the FDI-neutral, SEBI-regulated pathway; confirms shareholder dilution and pricing power was determined at the August 20 board meeting.
detail: The company allotted 2,505,219 equity securities to qualified institutional buyers (as defined under SEBI regulations) in a single tranche approved by the board on 20 August 2026. QIP is a SEBI-regulated mechanism permitting listed Indian companies to raise capital from institutional investors without a public offer prospectus, subject to pre-approval by shareholders and regulatory compliance. The allotment intimation to NSE is the formal disclosure triggering trading rights and lock-in obligations on the newly issued shares. Consideration amount and subscription price are not disclosed in the allotment notice.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, Reg. 75–88
framework.note: central; governs QIP pricing, disclosures, institutional investor eligibility and allotment process
central; permits issuance of shares by board resolution and shareholder approval requirements for preferential allotment
central; mandates QIP intimation to stock exchange and trading lock-in periods post-allotment

framework.ref: Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010, s. 5 (if QIP includes FPI capital)
framework.note: gate; requires no specific approval for FPI subscription in QIP if investor meets FEMA rules

framework.ref: Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, s. 5
framework.note: procedural; requires KYC/AML compliance for all institutional subscribers

conditions: Shareholder approval (prior to board approval, inferred from QIP regulatory requirement)
Qualified institutional buyer eligibility verification per SEBI QIP rules
Stock exchange allotment intimation within 2 days of board approval
structure.novel: None apparent; standard QIP closure sequence for listed tech companies post-shareholder mandate.

triggers.note: QIP issuance triggers pricing floor (volume weighted average price of prior 2 weeks) and lock-in (6 mo. for non-promoter, 1 yr. for promoter)
Allotment must be intimated to exchange within 2 business days; triggers regulatory disclosure and trading restrictions until lock-in expires
Board issuance of equity under shareholder authority; requires filing of return of allotment with Registrar of Companies within 30 days

firms.note: No legal advisor disclosed in the NSE allotment intimation; typical QIP would involve Tier-1 Indian corporate counsel and potentially international counsel if FPI involved.

firms.side: Subscriber counsel (not disclosed in NSE filing)
firms.note: Qualified institutional buyers typically self-represented or use internal counsel; no external counsel named in filing.
